issues.t: Air suspension leaks, sags or sits lopsided
issues.sym: The SUV sits low at one corner or all round, especially after standing overnight, the compressor runs a lot, or a suspension warning shows on the dash.
issues.why: The rubber air springs and seals perish with age and leak. A leak left alone wears out the compressor, and a failed height sensor can make one corner sit at the wrong height.
issues.next: Have the system leak-tested before replacing the compressor. Fix leaks early, and replace the air dryer/filter as part of the job.

issues.t: Coolant loss from slipped cylinder liner
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping with no visible leak, overheating, white exhaust smoke, or misfiring.
issues.why: On the 4.6L V8 the steel cylinder liners in the aluminum block can corrode and slip, letting coolant into places it shouldn't go.
issues.next: Stop driving if it overheats. A combustion-gas test of the coolant will show whether the liners or head gaskets are leaking. A slipped liner usually means a rebuilt engine.

issues.t: Head gasket leak
issues.sym: Losing coolant, overheating, white smoke from the exhaust, or a misfire.
issues.why: Head gasket failure is the most common cause of coolant loss on the 4.0L V8.
issues.next: Watch the temperature gauge and coolant level. Have a cooling system pressure test and combustion leak test done before the engine overheats badly.

issues.t: Body control module (BECM) faults
issues.sym: Alarm going off or immobilizing the engine, central locking or windows acting strangely, or several electrical items failing at once.
issues.why: The main body computer lives under the front passenger seat and can be damaged by water from spills or a damp interior.
issues.next: Check for water under the seat and dry it out. Have a Land Rover specialist read the body computer before replacing it.

issues.t: Heater blend motors fail
issues.sym: Wrong temperature from one side, heat stuck on hot or cold, or a clicking from behind the dash.
issues.why: The three blend motors that mix hot and cold air wear out, and replacing them all means taking the dash out.
issues.next: Have the climate system diagnosed to find which motor has failed. If the dash has to come out, consider doing all three and the heater core O-rings at once.

issues.t: Heater core O-ring leak into driver footwell
issues.sym: Wet carpet in the driver's footwell, a sweet coolant smell, foggy windows, or falling coolant level.
issues.why: The O-rings where the coolant pipes join the heater core perish with age and drip coolant into the cabin.
issues.next: Check under the carpet. Have the heater core O-rings replaced, a job of about three hours.

issues.t: Cracked flex-plate and loss of drive
issues.sym: Knocking or clattering from between the engine and gearbox, then the SUV won't move in any gear.
issues.why: Worn gearbox mounting bushings let the transmission sit out of line, which cracks the thin flex-plate that connects it to the engine.
issues.next: Have any new knock between engine and transmission checked right away. Replace the mountings at the same time as the flex-plate.

issues.t: Center differential viscous coupling wears out
issues.sym: Clunking or binding in tight turns, a whine from the transfer case, or slack in the drivetrain.
issues.why: The viscous coupling in the center differential wears out over time and can seize.
issues.next: Have the transfer case checked. A seized coupling makes the SUV bind in turns and strains the driveline.

issues.t: Underhood coolant and fluid leaks can start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: Coolant or fluid leaks in the engine bay, a burning smell, or smoke from under the hood.
issues.why: Several underhood hoses and connections could leak onto hot parts and ignite (NHTSA campaigns 98V149 and 00V328).
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Run the VIN for open recalls and have any underhood leak fixed right away.

issues.t: Water in transmission fluid can stop Park from holding (recall)
issues.sym: The SUV may roll even with the shifter in Park.
issues.why: Water could get into the transmission fluid and affect the park lock (NHTSA campaign 00V377).
issues.next: Always set the parking brake, and check the VIN for this recall.

issues.t: Air suspension sags overnight or shows a fault
issues.sym: The SUV is down on one corner or all round in the morning, the ride height is wrong, or a suspension fault message appears.
issues.why: Air springs, valve blocks, relief valves and pressure sensors fail with age. The compressor wears or shorts out if water gets into the spare wheel well, and a weak battery (under 11 volts) can also cause wrong ride height.
issues.next: Check the battery first, then have the system diagnosed with a Land Rover scan tool. Fixing a slow leak early saves the compressor.

issues.t: Timing chain guides wear and rattle
issues.sym: A rattling noise from the engine, often louder on startup.
issues.why: The plastic timing chain guides on the BMW-built 4.4L V8 become brittle and break apart. The job is hard and needs special tools.
issues.next: Have the noise diagnosed promptly. A broken guide can lead to serious engine damage.

issues.t: Timing chain rattle on cold start
issues.sym: A rattle for a second or two after a cold start that gets longer and louder over time, sometimes with cam timing codes P0016-P0019.
issues.why: The plastic chain guides and tensioner levers on the 5.0L V8 wear, letting the chains go slack. Land Rover released a bulletin to replace the tensioner and lever. Long oil change intervals make it worse.
issues.next: Don't wait. Have it checked before the chain jumps a tooth, which can wreck the engine.

issues.t: Supercharger coolant pump runs backwards
issues.sym: Reduced power or misfire under heavy load, with codes P0096 and/or P2601.
issues.why: Crossed wiring at the auxiliary coolant pump connector makes the pump run in reverse, so the engine computer cuts power to protect the engine.
issues.next: Have the pump and its wiring checked against Land Rover's bulletin. The fix is a new pump and corrected wiring.

issues.t: Transmission shifts badly or overheats
issues.sym: High revs, slow or reluctant shifts, a transmission overheat message after a long drive, or a gearbox warning.
issues.why: The corrosion inhibitor in old coolant can break down and partly block the transmission cooling tubes in the radiator. The automatic gearboxes in these trucks are also known to fail.
issues.next: Have the transmission and cooling system checked. Land Rover recommends changing the transmission fluid about every four years or 50,000 miles.

issues.t: Rear locking differential fault (P186D)
issues.sym: A transmission warning light, code P186D, or a "Transmission Fault Stop Safely" message.
issues.why: The electric motor that controls the rear locking differential can turn on while its brake is partly applied, which wears it out.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Land Rover's bulletin replaces the motor and updates the control software.

issues.t: Water leaks into the cabin
issues.sym: Wet carpets, damp headliner, water in the footwells, or the navigation and radio quitting after rain.
issues.why: Sunroof drain tubes can block, kink or come off, and the front door water shields may be badly fitted. Water can also reach the navigation unit.
issues.next: Clear the sunroof drains and check the door water shields. Dry the carpets quickly to protect the electronics under them.

issues.t: Rear suspension clunks over bumps
issues.sym: Clonking from the rear over bumps and potholes, and front ball joints wearing.
issues.why: The bushings in the rear hub carriers wear out early. Replacing them is a hard, time-consuming job.
issues.next: Have the rear suspension checked on a lift. Worn bushings also chew up tires.

issues.t: Water pump failure and coolant leaks
issues.sym: "Check Coolant Level" warnings, coolant puddles, a sweet smell, or the temperature climbing.
issues.why: Water pumps can fail without warning, and radiators and hoses leak with age. A faulty level sensor can also give false warnings.
issues.next: Check the coolant level when cold. Stop driving if it overheats; these aluminum engines don't tolerate overheating.

issues.t: Front driveshaft splines can wear and lose drive (recall)
issues.sym: Noise or vibration from the front driveline, grinding, and finally a loss of drive.
issues.why: The front differential coupling and propeller shaft were out of line, wearing the splines (NHTSA campaign 08V635).
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall; the dealer fits a revised shaft and flange kit.

issues.t: Front brake hoses can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: Brake fluid leaking at a front wheel, a soft pedal, and longer stops.
issues.why: The flexible front brake hoses could rupture (NHTSA campaign 15V039).
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check the VIN for open recalls; the dealer replaces both front hoses for free.

issues.t: Takata passenger airbag can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning. In a crash, the inflator can burst and throw metal fragments.
issues.why: The passenger airbag inflator degrades in heat and humidity (NHTSA campaigns 16V374, 17V015, 18V011 and 18V015).
issues.next: Check the VIN right away and get the free airbag replacement.

issues.t: Coolant crossover pipe leaks
issues.sym: Coolant loss, a sweet smell after driving, coolant warnings, or leaks around the thermostat housing.
issues.why: Plastic coolant pipes in the valley of the 5.0L V8 get brittle and crack or weep, often around 60,000 miles. Water pumps also fail.
issues.next: Keep an eye on the coolant level. Have leaks fixed before the engine overheats.

issues.t: Supercharger coupler rattle at idle
issues.sym: A metallic rattle or knock from the front of the engine at idle that is easy to confuse with timing chain noise, or a louder supercharger whine.
issues.why: The rubber isolator coupler in the supercharger snout wears with age and heat, and the snout bearings can run dry.
issues.next: Have a specialist tell this apart from timing chain noise. Replacing the coupler is a much smaller job than chain work.

issues.t: Oil and transmission cooler lines corrode and leak
issues.sym: Oil or transmission fluid drips under the front of the SUV.
issues.why: Road salt corrodes the metal oil and transmission cooler lines. Valve cover gaskets and the front crank seal also seep on older engines.
issues.next: Find the leak source and replace the line or gasket. Low transmission fluid can damage the gearbox.

issues.t: Diesel breather oil leaks
issues.sym: Oil misting or leaking around the engine breather, EGR valve or turbo.
issues.why: Breather oil leaks linked to the EGR valve and turbo are a known issue on these diesels. The fix is a modified breather pipe.
issues.next: Have the leak traced. Oil on hot exhaust parts can smoke or catch fire.

issues.t: Rotary gear selector doesn't rise
issues.sym: The rotary gear knob stays flush with the console when you start the SUV, so you can't select a gear easily.
issues.why: The rotary gear selector mechanism sometimes fails to rise.
issues.next: Restart the vehicle to see if it pops up. If it keeps happening, have the selector checked.

issues.t: Doors can look shut but be unlatched (recall)
issues.sym: A door appears closed but isn't latched and could open while driving.
issues.why: A fault in the soft-close keyless door latch system (NHTSA campaigns 15V385, 19V392 and 20V387).
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. Until fixed, pull each door to confirm it's latched.

issues.t: Front suspension knuckle can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Clunks from the front end or loose steering; in the worst case a suspension arm can come loose.
issues.why: The upper part of the front knuckle can crack (NHTSA campaigns 24V840, 25V514 and 26V527).
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls; the dealer fits a retaining bracket or a new knuckle.

issues.t: Surround-view rear camera fills with water (recall)
issues.sym: No picture, a distorted or misty picture when reversing.
issues.why: Water can get into the rear camera on models with the Surround Camera System (NHTSA campaign 24V023).
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall; the dealer adds a seal or replaces the camera.

issues.t: DC-DC converter overload can cut power (recall)
issues.sym: The 12-volt system stops charging, with possible loss of drive power and exterior lights while driving.
issues.why: On mild-hybrid models, a high electrical load can overload the DC-DC converter (NHTSA campaigns 26V248 and 26V599).
issues.next: Check the VIN for these recalls; the fix is a software update.

issues.t: Blocked cam carrier oil channel can cause oil leak (recall)
issues.sym: Oil leaking from the top of the engine, a burning oil smell, or smoke.
issues.why: An oil channel in the engine's cam carrier may be blocked, which can force oil out (NHTSA campaign 23V044).
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and stop if you smell burning oil.

issues.t: Rearview camera fogs or blanks from trapped water (recall)
issues.sym: A blank, foggy or distorted rearview camera picture.
issues.why: Water can get into or collect around the rear camera because the tailgate trim doesn't drain well (NHTSA campaigns 24V947 and 26V678).
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls; the dealer adds drain holes and replaces the camera if needed.

issues.t: Driver airbag clockspring connector can corrode (recall)
issues.sym: Possibly an airbag warning light; the driver airbag may not deploy correctly in a crash.
issues.why: The connector at the driver airbag clockspring can corrode over time (NHTSA campaign 26V389).
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall; the dealer treats the connector terminals.

issues.t: Panoramic sunroof side trim can come off (recall)
issues.sym: Wind noise or a loose strip of trim along the sunroof; the trim can fly off while driving.
issues.why: The side trim on the panoramic sunroof may not be secured properly (NHTSA campaign 26V097).
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall; the dealer inspects and secures the trim.
